Call for applications
The Call for applications provides information on the PhD programmes, positions and scholarships available for the upcoming PhD cycle. The Call also explains how to take part in the selection process and the mandatory deadlines.
The Call for Applications for admissions to the PhD programmes of the 42nd cycle is on line!
After reading it, please submit your application from the Apply@polito platform.
The selection process for admission to the PhD programmes is divided into three separate sessions. Candidates who have accepted a position in one session may not participate in subsequent sessions.

Positions and scholarships
Available positions are divided into:
Regular positions
positions with a scholarship and open research topic;
positions with scholarships for specific research topic;
positions offered in apprenticeship format;
positions without a scholarship and open research topic;
positions without a scholarship for specific research topic.
Reserved positions
positions reserved for recipients of scholarships awarded by foreign governments;
positions reserved for the Project POLITO FOR REFUGEES;
positions reserved for the Project CONFLICT ZONES;
positions reserved for specific international initiatives;
positions reserved to Research Fellows.
Positions available for the second session of the 42nd cycle
Politecnico di Torino makes available, for the 42nd cycle, funding corresponding to a minimum of 110 PhD scholarships.
These PhD positions will be distributed between the three sessions, as detailed in the table below, which is integral part of the Call. Additional PhD positions with their specific details may become available after the publication of the Call and will be indicated in the aforementioned table, which will therefore be updated, providing evidence exclusively through this website
An update on the available positions for the first session of the 42nd cycle will be published every Tuesday and Friday. Therefore, the absence of positions at a given moment should not be interpreted as a definitive absence of positions for the ongoing session.
The definite number of positions available for each session and each PhD programme will be finalized in the present page within 6 days before the date of the oral interviews set by each Admissions Committee and published in accordance with the provisions set in art. 14 of the Call.
For the positions with a predefined research topic and for the positions offered in apprenticeship format, applicants can find the information sheet by clicking on the number of the positions available.

Special Projects
Project POLITO FOR REFUGEES
In order to promote concrete actions of solidarity and support for students with international protection status (refugees or beneficiaries of subsidiary protection), Politecnico di Torino is reserving, within the second session of the 42nd cycle, 1 doctoral position for candidates with international protection (refugee status or beneficiaries of subsidiary protection) who hold a second-level academic degree obtained in Italy or abroad that qualifies them for admission to a doctoral program, in accordance with the requirements set forth in Article 7 of the Call (see Attachment 1.A).
Project CONFLICT ZONES
In order to promote concrete initiatives of solidarity and support, Politecnico di Torino may make PhD positions with scholarships available to international students who are foreign nationals, hold a foreign qualification that grants access to doctoral programmes, and reside in and come from countries affected by armed conflict.
The list of countries recognized by the University as being affected by conflict is available at the following link: Conflict-affected Countries list | Politecnico di Torino.
As part of this initiative, and in order to give effect to the testamentary wishes of Ms Josephine Teresa Pratt, Politecnico di Torino may also reserve PhD positions with scholarships for Afghan nationals who meet the requirements set out in Attachment 1.B of the Call.
In particular, within the second session of the 42nd cycle, 2 PhD positions with scholarships are available, one of which is funded through the Pratt Legacy.
